Name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting
Title: When to Retrieve Is Only a Budget Question: A Harm-Mass Bound on the Value of Retrieval Timing for Experience Memory, Tested at Two Distractor Levels, With Failure-Keyed Retrieval at Stall Against Planted Recoveries, Coverage-Matched Self Detours and a Compiled Rulebook
Short Hypothesis: With retrieved content, cached prefix and message format held fixed, the value of any retrieval-timing policy (start, fixed schedule, on stall, learned) over always-retrieve is bounded above by the harm mass: the fraction of episodes on which retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt solves, beyond test-retest flips. On ALFWorld we measure the harm mass as a paired-table estimand at two distractor levels of one expert bank and predict it is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with mislabelled twins; stall-triggered retrieval then sits within +/-8 of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions and, at the twin bank, gains over always-retrieve by at least 8 net but never more than the harm mass plus the floor, so timing re-trades uncached tokens for the same success and cannot buy more. A failure-keyed query at stall beats a content-free key only when the bank holds matching recoveries: at matched coverage the agent's own curated detours do as well as planted recoveries, the natural self pool does not, and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost.
Related Work: arXiv:2607.24010 (When Should Active RAG Retrieve?) recasts active retrieval as marginal correctness over the no-retrieval answer under a budget, but on QA with document retrieval, without a harm-mass estimand on paired seeds, a stall trigger or caching costs. ProactAgent (arXiv:2604.20572, 'Ask Only When Needed') retrieves proactively from memory and skills for lifelong agents without an always-retrieve-at-matched-content arm or an upper bound on the decision. FLARE (arXiv:2305.06983) and Adaptive-RAG (arXiv:2403.14403) trigger retrieval by uncertainty or complexity in QA. Reflexion (arXiv:2303.11366) conditions on failure across trials, not within-episode stalls, and has no static control. Digest: arXiv:2607.07380 (hidden-state uncertainty decides when to retrieve; no always/never baselines), s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (RL proxy decides when/how; cost unaccounted), arXiv:2510.16724 (survey; no common protocol), arXiv:2607.20972 (cue-triggered deterministic injection beats voluntary reads; no harm bound or compiled control), arXiv:2505.00234 (self-generated examples for sequential decision tasks, the on-policy bank). Archived ideas do not address timing; compile_dont_retrieve concerns the goal-conditioned read at episode start.
Abstract: Adaptive retrieval papers ask when to retrieve but do not report what a perfect answer to that question would be worth. For experience memory under prompt caching the accounting is simple: with the retrieved content, the cached prefix and the message format held fixed, a timing policy can add success over always-retrieve only on episodes where retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt would have solved. We call that fraction the harm mass and measure it as a pre-registered paired-table estimand on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, static3 cached prefix from Measurement C, one k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 or later): P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) minus the same discordance between two static runs, at two distractor levels of one expert bank (natural, and a 1:1 mislabelled-twin bank in which goal-keyed retrieval returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the slots). Predictions: the harm mass is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with twins; stall-triggered retrieval (two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated action) is within +/-8 of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions; at the twin bank it gains over always-retrieve by at least 8 net and by no more than the harm mass plus the floor, and a fixed step-10 schedule does the same as the trigger. We then ask whether the query at stall matters, separating key from content in a k=1 2x2 (failure key vs random key; planted-recovery bank vs expert pool) and manipulating recovery coverage in the agent's own detour pool (natural coverage measured by a validated tagger; curated recovery windows at coverage near 1). Predictions: the failure key beats a random key only with planted recoveries; curated self detours match planted recoveries at matched coverage while the natural pool falls short; and a ~200-token recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost. The output is an accuracy-cost frontier on which the timing decision moves along the frontier rather than above it, with the bound tested as an inequality at a level where it binds and a test of whether any query is more than decorative at stall time.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: ALFWorld 274 games x 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching. Shared prefix: static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached), the best static arm from Measurement C; every arm sits on it. Retrieval block: k=3 goal-keyed items (~430 tokens) appended as one environment-style message with identical text and format whether appended at step 0 (always), at step 10 (schedule) or at the stall (stall arms), so content, prefix and format are fixed across timing arms and only the delivery step varies. Banks: natural expert bank; distractor bank = the expert bank plus one mislabelled twin per item (the item's goal sentence attached to the trajectory of a different-type expert item that shares the target object), so goal-keyed retrieval ties twins with originals and returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the k=3 slots (Measurement C's wrong-type placebo blind1 is -3 under k0, about -15 under static3, the reason to expect harm); planted-recovery bank (five ALFWorld failure modes: closed receptacle, wrong receptacle, object already held, wrong object instance, missing 'go to'; one ~40-token recovery item each, keyed by failure text; coverage 1.0 by construction); self pool = 1,892 self-generated successes with detours, indexed by failed-action windows (natural level), and its curated subset of windows the tagger marks as a failure mode followed by a recovery within three steps (curated level). Coverage c(pool) = fraction of stall-firing episodes (from cell 4's firing log) whose tagged failure mode has at least one same-mode recovery window in the pool; the rule-based tagger reads the last three actions and observations and is validated on 100 hand-labelled stall windows (agreement >= 0.8 required before the self-pool cells run). Where the expert bank exceeds the ~80-item whole-context limit, the truncated whole-bank arm is Measurement C's k-sweep (k7 = +19.5 over static3) and the start read is held fixed at k=3 here. Stall trigger: first occurrence of two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated (observation, action) pair; threshold 2 confirmatory, threshold 5 optional. Queries at stall: goal sentence (k=3, matching always); failure key = last three actions and observations (k=1); random key = uniform draw from the pool (k=1); k=1 for all failure-key and random-key cells because the planted bank holds one item per mode. Estimand for P1 on the 548 (game, seed) rows: D(L) = P(static3_A succeeds and always(L) fails), D0 = P(static3_A succeeds and static3_B fails), Delta_harm(L) = D(L) - D0, with static3_A the Measurement C cell and static3_B a fresh re-run; cluster-bootstrap CI over games. The cross-fitted oracle (decide on static3_A, score static3_B where it succeeded and always elsewhere) is computed from the same cells and reported as a descriptive upper bound; no oracle cell is run. Cells (548 episodes each, ~30 min per cell with both replicas busy): (1) static3_B re-run; (2) always-natural; (3) always-distractor; (4) stall goal-key k=3 threshold 2, natural; (5) stall goal-key k=3 threshold 2, distractor; (6) step-10 schedule goal-key k=3, natural; (7) stall failure-key k=1, expert pool; (8) stall failure-key k=1, planted; (9) stall random-key k=1, planted; (10) stall failure-key k=1, self natural; (11) stall failure-key k=1, self curated; (12) static3 + recovery rulebook (the five planted items concatenated, ~200 tokens, cached; the whole-bank arm of the planted bank); (13) rulebook + stall failure-key k=1 planted. Optional if time remains: (14) curated-self whole-bank arm, cached, truncated to the top-N recovery windows by tag confidence, type-balanced, that fit 16k with the longest trajectory (the brief's whole-bank rule; exploratory); (15) stall goal-key threshold 5, natural. Arithmetic: 13 confirmatory cells x 548 = 7,124 episodes, ~3.25 h wall on two A100s; with both optional cells 8,220 episodes, ~3.75 h; inside the original 4 h envelope. Logging per episode and arm: success, steps, firing step, uncached prefill tokens (prompt tokens minus cached tokens from vLLM), cache hit rate; accuracy vs uncached tokens per episode is the cost axis. Pre-registered order: cells 1-3 (P1 decides whether the distractor level exists), then 4-6 (P2, P6), then 8, 9, 7 (P3), then 10-11 (P4), then 12-13 (P5), then the optional cells.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: never-retrieve = static3 (cached; the best static arm from Measurement C, +12.4 over k0); always-retrieve = static3 plus the same k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 (uncached block, ~430 tokens per episode; its residual over static3_B is checked against Measurement C's +17.2 +/- 5); fixed step-10 schedule (timing without a trigger); random-key-at-stall on the planted bank (content-free key, pool fixed); failure-key-at-stall on the expert pool (key fixed, no recovery content); compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix (the static counterpart of planted retrieval and the whole-bank arm of the 5-item planted bank); curated-self whole-bank arm (cached, truncated; optional); cross-fitted oracle computed from static3_A, static3_B and always (descriptive upper bound, no cell). Type conditioning: every arm shares the static3 prefix, so type conditioning is constant in every contrast; the rulebook and planted items are keyed by failure mode, not task type; Measurement C's instr_all (type-agnostic, -20.1 under k3) and blind1 (wrong type) are the standing references. Manipulated properties, two levels each on one environment: distractor rate of the expert bank (natural vs 1:1 mislabelled twins) for the harm mass; recovery coverage of the self pool (natural c_nat vs curated c_cur, both measured) for the failure key. Ablations: rulebook with vs without stall retrieval on top (P5); stall threshold 2 vs 5 (optional); step-10 schedule vs stall trigger (P2 secondary).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline; harm mass small at the natural bank, large with distractors): Estimand Delta_harm(L) = P(static3_A succeeds and always(L) fails) - P(static3_A succeeds and static3_B fails) on the same 548 rows, cluster-bootstrap CI over games. Prediction: Delta_harm(natural) < 8 points and Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8 points. Falsified if Delta_harm(natural) >= 8 (retrieval from the natural expert bank breaks more than 8 percent of static-solved episodes beyond test-retest, so timing policies have headroom at the natural bank and the 'inside the floor' clause is wrong; producible: Measurement C's look-at type is +4.8 with CI including 0 and pick types +10 to +12, so a harm mass of 8 to 12 points concentrated on pick and look-at episodes is reachable) or if Delta_harm(distractor) < 8 (the reader ignores mislabelled twins, the high level failed as a manipulation, P6 is not run). Arms: static3_A (Measurement C), static3_B re-run, always-natural, always-distractor. The estimand is compared with a threshold, not with any cell it is built from; the run oracle is dropped.
- P2 (timing is budgeting at the natural bank; two-sided): stall goal-key (threshold 2, k=3, natural) is within +/-8 net of always-natural. Falsified if below by more than 8 net (the stall arrives after the step budget is spent) or above by more than 8 net (with the same items, prefix and format, reading after exploration beats reading at start: timing adds value beyond harm avoidance, which P1's Delta_harm(natural) < 8 cannot supply). Cost axis: uncached prefill tokens per episode; pre-registered expectation that the stall arm fires on at most 50 percent of episodes; a higher firing rate is a detector-selectivity failure reported on the cost axis, not a falsifier of the accuracy prediction. Secondary: the step-10 schedule is within +/-8 of the stall arm; falsified if the schedule falls below the stall arm by more than 8 net (the trigger's information matters beyond its firing count).
- P6 (the bound binds at the distractor level; run only if Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8): stall goal-key (threshold 2, k=3, distractor bank) exceeds always-distractor by at least 8 net and by at most Delta_harm(distractor) + 8. Falsified if the gain exceeds Delta_harm(distractor) + 8 (a timing policy adds value beyond avoiding harm with content held fixed: the core claim is wrong) or if the gain is below 8 net (the trigger also fires on static-solved episodes, so it does not realize the harm avoidance that is available: the bound survives but stall retrieval is not a budgeting device). Arms: stall-goal-distractor vs always-distractor, with Delta_harm(distractor) from P1; the stall cell is a separate run, so neither inequality is algebraic.
- P3 (failure key needs matching content; positive control with key and content separated): at stall with k=1, failure-key retrieval from the planted bank exceeds random-key retrieval from the planted bank by at least 8 net (key varies, pool fixed) and exceeds failure-key retrieval from the expert pool by at least 8 net (pool varies, key fixed). Falsified if either difference is below 8 net: the first means the failure text does not index the recovery or the reader does not apply a 40-token hint mid-episode (random-key finds the right item on 20 percent of firings, so the reachable gap is 80 percent of the per-hint effect); the second means expert trajectory segments already carry the recovery. If the first clause fails, P4 and P5 are reported as uninterpretable.
- P4 (self-pool recovery coverage manipulated): two levels, natural self pool (c_nat measured) and curated self pool (recovery-tagged windows only; c_cur measured, expected >= 0.8), failure key, k=1. Prediction: the curated pool is within +/-8 net of failure-key planted retrieval, and the natural pool is below the curated pool by at least 8 net. Falsified if curated is below planted by more than 8 net (the agent's own detours are unusable as recoveries even when present and indexed, so the failure key needs compiled content) or if natural is within +/-8 of curated (the natural pool already delivers recoveries by the failure key, so the key is load-bearing with natural content, contradicting the hypothesis). Guard: if c_nat >= 0.8 the two levels differ only in distractor windows and the natural-vs-curated contrast tests distractor load; the hypothesis clause is then scored by natural vs planted directly (falsified if within +/-8). If c_cur < 0.8 the curated clause is exploratory. Arms: cells 10 and 11 against cell 8.
- P5 (rulebook matches retrieval; conditional on P3's first clause clearing the floor): static3 + rulebook (cached, whole planted bank) is within +/-8 net of failure-key planted retrieval at stall, and rulebook + planted stall retrieval adds less than 8 net over the rulebook alone. Falsified if planted retrieval beats the rulebook by 8 net or more (recovery must be delivered at the moment of failure rather than read from the prefix) or if rulebook + retrieval exceeds the rulebook by 8 net or more (delivery position adds value even with the content in the prefix). Content is identical by construction; the only channel is delivery position, which the rulebook + retrieval cell instruments. Arms: cells 12 and 13 against cell 8.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) rows with identical seeds across arms; primary outcome task success; net differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs over 274 games; +/-8-net floor pre-registered at 274 x 2; margins as fractions of the Measurement C retrieval gain (+17.2, CI half-width about 5). Delta_harm is a single pre-registered estimand computed from the paired table with the static3_A vs static3_B test-retest discordance subtracted, with a cluster-bootstrap CI; the McNemar discordant cells are reported alongside; the run oracle is not used as an estimator and no oracle cell is run. Positive controls that must clear the floor before any null is interpreted: always-natural minus static3_B >= +8 (expected +17.2 +/- 5 per Measurement C; a shortfall is reported against that value, not against zero); Delta_harm(distractor) >= 8 before P6; P3's planted gain >= 8 before P4 and P5. Shared cells disclosed: P1 and P2 both reference always-natural, so its noise moves Delta_harm(natural) and stall-minus-always in the same direction (toward P1's falsifier and P2's upper falsifier together); P3, P4 and P5 all reference the failure-key planted cell (8). Tagger validated on 100 hand-labelled stall windows (agreement >= 0.8) before the self-pool cells; c_nat and c_cur reported with the tagger's confusion matrix. Stall arms log firing rate and step-at-fire; cost is uncached prefill tokens per episode from vLLM logs; cache hit rate verified for static3, rulebook and whole-bank arms. P1-P6 and the cell order pre-registered before cell 1; per-type numbers and the optional cells are exploratory.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The mislabelled-twin bank may not produce harm if the reader ignores wrong-type trajectories (Delta_harm(distractor) < 8); then the high level is unavailable and P6 is not run, which is reported; a second construction (wrong-type items with rewritten goals) is the next attempt and is out of this budget. The stall definition is heuristic; if it fires on more than half the episodes the cost saving is lost while the accuracy prediction still stands; the step budget may make late retrieval useless (P2's lower falsifier, itself informative). The failure-mode tagger may be unreliable on some modes; its agreement is gated before the self-pool cells. The self pool's recovery windows may be too rare for some modes (c_cur < 0.8), in which case the curated level is not coverage-matched to the planted bank and P4's curated clause is exploratory. ALFWorld has only five recurring failure modes, which favours the rulebook; this is the claim but limits generality, and WebShop (different failure modes, a day of setup) is the stated extension. The cross-fitted oracle uses outcome information and is descriptive, not deployable. vLLM seed reproducibility is imperfect; static3_B quantifies it and it is subtracted from Delta_harm. Learned timing policies are not trained; the claim is that no policy with the same content can exceed the harm mass, tested on stall and schedule policies at two harm levels.
Addresses gap: G14 (value of the retrieval decision quantified against always-retrieve, never-retrieve and a fixed schedule at accounted per-episode cost, with a harm-mass upper bound measured at two distractor levels so the bound is tested where it binds); secondary G15 (whether a failure-keyed query is more than decorative depends on measured recovery coverage, planted, curated-self and natural, and whether compiled instructions match it).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Retrieval on this node (Measurement A): k=0 0.536/0.549 -> k=3 0.807/0.869' and Measurement C's k3 - static3 = +17.2 measure always-retrieve at start; this idea claims the value of any timing decision with the same content is bounded by a quantity those cells cannot see (the mass of static-solved episodes that retrieval breaks, beyond test-retest), measures it as a paired-table estimand, and manipulates it with a distractor bank so the bound is tested as an inequality rather than as a null. Digest card arxiv:2607.07380 decides when to retrieve from hidden-state uncertainty without always/never baselines; this idea claims and tests that no decision policy can beat always-retrieve by more than the measured harm mass, and that the failure key's value tracks measured recovery coverage (planted, curated-self, natural) and is compilable into a cached rulebook. None of the four archived ideas concerns timing; compile_dont_retrieve addresses the goal-conditioned read at start, which is held fixed at k=3 on the static3 prefix here; distractor rate and recovery coverage are manipulated, not named.
Changes made: P1 (headline, was near_entailed): the run oracle-decision cell is dropped; a single pre-registered estimand Delta_harm = P(static_A succeeds and always fails) - P(static_A succeeds and static_B fails), computed from the paired table with a cluster-bootstrap CI and calibrated by the static test-retest discordance as the fix asks, replaces the two incompatible versions; the cross-fitted oracle is reported descriptively only, from existing cells. Harm is now manipulated (natural bank vs 1:1 mislabelled-twin distractor bank), so P1 predicts a small mass at one level and a large one at the other, and the bound is tested as an inequality where it binds (new P6: stall gain over always lies between 8 and Delta_harm + 8; the upper falsifier is timing adding value beyond harm avoidance). This keeps the claim as sharp as before or sharper: the original tested the bound only as a null inside the floor. P2 (open but one-sided): the falsifier is now two-sided (stall above always by more than 8 falsifies 'timing is only budgeting'); firing rate moved from falsifier to a pre-registered cost-axis manipulation check; all timing arms share the static3 prefix and an identical appended block so content, prefix and format are fixed and only the delivery step varies. P3 (open, key and bank confounded): replaced by a k=1 2x2 (failure key vs random key; planted bank vs expert pool) so key and content are separated; always-retrieve is no longer P3's reference. P4 (near_entailed): recovery coverage is measured (validated tagger; c_nat, c_cur reported) and manipulated (natural vs curated self pool) as the fix asks; the prediction is restated with falsifiers in both directions (curated below planted by more than 8: self detours unusable; natural within 8 of curated: the failure key is load-bearing with natural content) plus a guard for c_nat >= 0.8. P5 (open): cells unchanged; made explicitly conditional on P3's planted gain clearing the floor (shared-term P3-P5). Baseline aligned with Measurement C: static3 is the shared cached prefix and never-retrieve arm; always-natural minus static3 is checked against +17.2 +/- 5. Whole-bank rule: the rulebook is the planted bank's whole-bank arm; a curated-self whole-bank arm is added as optional. Cut to fit: observation-key cells, self goal-key cell, always re-run, run-oracle cell, k=1 vs k=3 and indexing ablations; threshold 5 optional. 13 confirmatory + 2 optional cells x 548 episodes, ~3.75 h on two A100s. Refused: did not drop the 'natural self pool is decorative' clause or soften the bound into a measurement study; both remain predictions with named falsifying arms.
